newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says Feb sales rise in 4 countries.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says Feb sales rise in 4 countries.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Thursday its February car sales surged in Britain, France, Austria and Switzerland, compared with the same month a year earlier.

In Britain, sales leapt 38.9 percent to 3,376 cars in the month, while the total market in the country rose 2.4 percent. In the first two months of the year, Volvo's British car sales rose 32.8 percent to 7,086 vehicles.
"In Britain we noted a sales increase in all model groups," Volvo spokesman Ulf Thorne told Reuters.
"The S40/V40 increased to 1,300 in February and the 'new' S70/V70 sold 29 percent better than the 'old' 850 series."
The upgraded S70/V70 was sold for the first time in Britain in February.
In France, the company's car sales jumped 33.3 percent to 565 cars in February, Thorne said.
In the first two months of the year, its French sales rose 27.8 percent to 1,108 cars.

In Austria, Volvo sold 93.2 percent more cars in February, with sales totalling 313 cars. In January and February combined, its sales rose 19.2 percent to 534 cars, while the total market fell four percent.
In Switzerland, Volvo's sales rose 26.6 percent to 442 cars last month.
But the company sold 2.6 percent fewer cars in the first two months of the year, down to 798, while the total Swiss market fell 8.9 percent.
"For all these markets the upturn stems from the access of the S40/V40 model and the good reception of the S70/V70," Thorne said.
